Open-Meteo mode samples one model cell in each of the 8 directions around you (9 cells, centre included) — a cell\'s position is its compass direction. WAQI mode takes the 9 nearest monitoring stations: nearest in the centre, then clockwise by distance, with no radius limit.
Wear a fitted N95 / KN95 and shorten time outdoors
Stay indoors and avoid outdoor activity

The three levels map only to AQI ranges (0–100 / 101–200 / ≥201). This is not medical advice. If PM2.5 dominates, a fitted N95 / KN95 is recommended. Sensitive groups, children, the elderly and people with heart or lung disease should follow official guidance and their own symptoms.
CN mode uses a single OM source, no comparison

The two sources are not interchangeable. OM is a CAMS model grid with local 24h/8h/1h averaging; WAQI derives an equivalent concentration from published station sub-indices and recomputes with EPA 2024 (derived, ±2 AQI). Levels may disagree; the status bar follows the primary source only.
US AQI: Open-Meteo / CAMS by default, EPA 2024 breakpoints, local averaging. Optional WAQI recalculation. CN AQI: Open-Meteo / CAMS, HJ 633-2012, local averaging

Source: Open-Meteo / CAMS · HJ 633-2012 · local 24h/8h averaging

Live estimate, not an official published AQI. Concentrations are averaged over the windows the breakpoint table requires (US EPA 2024: PM2.5/PM10 24h, O₃/CO 8h, NO₂/SO₂ 1h) before lookup. Feeding an instantaneous peak into 24h breakpoints inflates the result badly. Open-Meteo is a CAMS model grid, so values differ from ground monitors and from aqicn / AirNow by source, averaging window and observation time; they cannot validate each other. aqicn still uses EPA 2012 breakpoints (122 µg/m³ → 185 instead of 198).

US: primary source is OM local 2024 — raw Open-Meteo concentrations computed with US EPA 2024 breakpoints (PM2.5 9.0 / 35.4 / 55.4 / 125.4 / 225.4 / 325.4 / 500.4). Concentrations are averaged over 24h/8h/1h first. No token needed. Most online converters, including aqicn, still use the 2012 table and read lower for the same concentration.
CN: the same Open-Meteo concentrations computed with HJ 633-2012, averaged over 24h/8h first. No token, single source, no comparison. Model grid data may differ from ground monitors.

Why is this different from aqicn or the official site? This app reads Open-Meteo CAMS model grid data, while aqicn and AirNow read ground monitors. Source, spatial coverage and observation time all differ, so the numbers never match. aqicn also still uses EPA 2012 breakpoints, which read lower. You can switch the primary source or enable the WAQI recalculation for comparison, but the two rows are not validation of each other.

Follows the primary source by default. Open-Meteo gives model grid cells of about 45 km with no station names; WAQI gives real monitoring stations with names and distances, at the cost of 8 extra requests per refresh.
WAQI ground station, recalculated with the 2024 breakpoints

This is a real monitoring station, but the number is not the station\'s own reported value: the app inverts the published 2012 sub-index to an equivalent PM2.5 concentration and recalculates it with the US EPA 2024 breakpoints. It will differ by a few points from what aqicn shows, because the scales differ.
The grid is ordered by distance: the centre is the nearest station, then clockwise from the top are the 2nd to 9th nearest. A cell\'s position means distance, not direction.
Same value as the centre station: neighbouring stations often sit in the same pollution episode, and differences under 1 get rounded away.
Area = %2$d monitoring stations within %1$d km, median %3$d (range %4$d–%5$d); each station is recalculated with the 2024 breakpoints.
Area = %2$d monitoring stations within %1$d km, worst %3$d (range %4$d–%5$d); the median is lower; each station is recalculated with the 2024 breakpoints.
Stations measure at ground level and are strongly affected by siting (kerbside, park, rooftop); a 20-point gap between neighbours is normal and does not mean one is wrong.
